arms.name: random_scaled_ema
arms.purpose: conservative allocation control receives one additional step and greater cost

mechanism.backward: existing gathered active-row-only FFN dgrad/wgrad at 87.5%, with all returned FFN-path gradients multiplied by 1/activity
mechanism.random_interpretation: uniform exact-budget row sampling with inverse-probability scaling gives an unbiased sparse-gradient estimator
mechanism.low_max_abs_interpretation: the same variance correction is applied, but deterministic low_max_abs selection is not claimed to be unbiased
mechanism.ema: identical final 0.95 EMA for every arm with no decay sweep or checkpoint selection
mechanism.deployment: ordinary dense inference with averaged weights

cost_accounting.training: same realized-row CPU-calibrated FFN sparse-backward formula as the unscaled 87.5% experiment
cost_accounting.scale_aux: one multiplication per returned FFN input gradient, weight gradient, and bias gradient element, included separately
cost_accounting.ema_aux: two estimated operations per parameter per step for every arm
cost_accounting.evaluation: reported separately and excluded from training-plus-EMA cost

primary_endpoint: final EMA ordinary dense held-out loss at training-plus-scaling-plus-EMA cost

decision_rules.allocation_failure: scaled low_max_abs EMA does not beat scaled random despite random receiving more steps and cost; stop
decision_rules.no_level_3: scaled low_max_abs beats random but not dense EMA; stop
decision_rules.development_level_3: scaled low_max_abs EMA loss is below random and dense EMA while total cost is no greater than either
decision_rules.confirmation: only development_level_3 launches the identical body-7 comparison

prohibited: combining this shot with attention projection sparsity
changing scale, activity, EMA decay, steps, or evaluation after launch
launching body 7 without a development-level win
